title: Condition failures against the reference, classified by shape
question: Why do the Sonnet and Haiku passes fail the conditions field far more often than the Opus passes?
method: Every core-matched pair whose full-tier failure includes conditions, in the six pass-against-reference comparisons, classified by the shape of the two condition trees (added, omitted, different premise references, repeated restrictions).
conclusion: The main Sonnet condition failure is a condition tree on a claim the reference leaves unconditioned (definientia conditioned on the definition's premise; premises carrying their own restrictions): a convention the guideline does not state, not a misreading of the text.
